observations: Three photos show multiple electronic keyboards wrapped in plastic, standing upright on a tiled floor.
The keyboards have 61 keys, typical of portable or mini keyboards.
The keyboards vary in design: some have a black and white color scheme, others are silver or light gray, and one has a blue and white panel with a control wheel and buttons.
The plastic wrapping is crinkled and appears to be new or lightly used.
No brand or model name is visible on any keyboard in any photo.
The background includes a wall with a pipe and a fan, suggesting a storage or workshop area.
The watermark 'MARY OLUGBAMI POSTED ON JIJI' is present on all photos.

claims.evidence: No brand or model is visible to assess quality or price. The term 'quality' is subjective and cannot be verified from photos alone.
No photo shows the keyboard powered on or in use. The keys and buttons are not visible in operation. The plastic wrapping may hide damage or non-functionality.
No adapter is visible in any photo. The claim cannot be confirmed without seeing the adapter or its connection to the keyboard.

claims.claim: Bought from the UK, no dead key, no crackle.
claims.evidence: No photo shows this; it is the seller's word only.

risks.risk: Keyboard may not be functional (keys/buttons not working)
risks.proof: A video or photo showing the keyboard powered on, with keys being pressed and sound produced.
Photo of the adapter connected to the keyboard or showing its presence.

risks.risk: Hidden damage or wear under plastic wrapping
risks.proof: Close-up photos of the keyboard without plastic, showing keys, buttons, and casing for cracks, dents, or wear.

proof_requests: Close-up of the keyboard's screen showing the brand and model.
Video or photo of the keyboard powered on, showing keys being pressed and sound produced.
Photo of the adapter connected to the keyboard.
Close-up photos of the keyboard without plastic, showing all keys, buttons, and casing for damage.
response.reason: What the item is shows, but not the model that sets its price: no photo shows it clearly enough to read. The shot asked for first would settle it.
